sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT BOOKS THE OTHER CALLER READS FOR ENJOYMENT OR SELF-IMPROVEMENT.         DO YOU HAVE SIMILAR OR DIFFERENT INTERESTS IN BOOKS?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: This is Sarah, we talked on the line before?
ParticipantB: Yeah, sure. It's Jen.
ParticipantA: Oh, hi Jen! How are you doing?
ParticipantB: Good, good. Just wrapping up a job at the old mill.
ParticipantA: That sounds intense. What do you do for a living?
ParticipantB: Electrician. Been doing it for about five years now.
ParticipantA: Nice. I'm an accountant. I spend my days staring at spreadsheets, you know?
ParticipantB: Oh, really? I figure those people just deal with taxes and headaches.
ParticipantA: Well, it's actually kind of fascinating if you look at it the right way.
ParticipantB: Hmm. I never really saw it that way.
ParticipantA: Like, I had this one client last year who was losing his business because of a tiny decimal error.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I guess that happens.
ParticipantA: And fixing it saved him thousands, but it felt like solving a mystery. It makes you think.
ParticipantB: I suppose. I think numbers are just numbers, though. Too rigid.
ParticipantA: Maybe for you, but for me, finding the pattern is the whole point. It's like detective work.
ParticipantB: I guess I prefer the physical stuff. Wires, circuits. You can touch them.
ParticipantA: True. I love that about your job. I wish I could touch my spreadsheets sometimes.
ParticipantB: Nah, I don't think I'd enjoy sitting behind a desk. Too quiet for me.
ParticipantA: Absolutely. So, what kinds of books do you read when you get off work?
ParticipantB: Honestly? Not many. Maybe something quick to unwind.
ParticipantA: Oh, I see. I read a lot. Mostly historical fiction or stuff about business.
ParticipantB: Historical? Interesting. I usually just grab whatever is on the top shelf.
ParticipantA: Like, did you read anything good lately?
ParticipantB: Um, I think I started this thing about wiring houses in the 19th century.
ParticipantA: Oh wow. That sounds heavy. Is it good?
ParticipantB: Eh. Kind of dry. But I suppose I should read more about people's lives.
ParticipantA: You should! Stories can actually teach you a lot, even if they're just made up.
ParticipantB: Maybe. I'll keep that in mind. I'm usually too tired after climbing ladders to read.
ParticipantA: I get that. Sometimes I just stare at the ceiling after crunching numbers.
ParticipantB: Yeah, exactly. Same thing.
ParticipantA: Well, maybe you'll pick up a book next time. I'd love to hear what you think.
ParticipantB: Sure, maybe. Thanks for talking, Sarah.
ParticipantA: No problem, Jen. Take care.
ParticipantB: You too. Bye.
